project.name: engflow
project.description: EngFlow is an online self-study language learning platform (English) built with Spring Boot for the backend and Vue.js 3 + Vite + Pinia + Tailwind CSS for the frontend, using Microsoft SQL Server and Redis on Docker.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand EngFlow's purpose as an online self-study English learning platform. It explains the full tech stack — Spring Boot backend, Vue 3 + Vite + Pinia + Tailwind CSS frontend, SQL Server and Redis on Docker — and provides setup instructions for Docker, Maven, and npm.

tour.title: Infrastructure & Orchestration
tour.description: Docker Compose defines the two infrastructure services the platform depends on: Microsoft SQL Server with a health-checked initialisation script and Redis for caching. The .env file supplies the secrets (SA_PASSWORD, JWT_SECRET) that both Docker and Spring Boot consume at runtime.

tour.title: Backend Entry Point & Configuration
tour.description: EngflowApplication.java, annotated with @SpringBootApplication, bootstraps the entire backend. The main() method calls SpringApplication.run, and a CommandLineRunner bean logs Flyway detection at startup. application.properties ties everything together: SQL Server datasource, Hibernate DDL auto-update, Redis connection, JWT secret and expiration, CORS origins, and Flyway disable.

tour.title: Database Schema
tour.description: The Flyway migration V1__init_schema.sql creates all 9 core tables: users, lessons, vocabulary, grammar, exercises, user_progress, exercise_submissions, achievements, and user_achievements. These tables are the foundation every entity, repository, and service layer builds upon. Indexes on foreign keys and lookup columns optimise the most frequent queries.

tour.title: JPA Data Models
tour.description: Lesson.java and User.java are the two central JPA entities. Lesson holds one-to-many relationships to vocabularies, grammars, and exercises, plus level/category metadata. User carries authentication fields, role (USER/ADMIN), points, and study streak tracking. Together they define the domain vocabulary every other layer uses.

tour.title: Data Access Layer
tour.description: Spring Data JPA repositories provide the abstraction between business logic and the database. UserRepository offers findByEmail, findByUsername, and existence checks — used by the authentication flow. LessonRepository supplies custom queries for published lessons, level filtering, and detail fetching that power the lesson listing and detail views.

tour.title: Business Logic Services
tour.description: The service implementations contain EngFlow's core business logic. LessonServiceImpl (the highest fan-out node in the graph) assembles composite lesson responses with nested vocabularies, grammars, and exercises, enriching them with per-user progress data. UserServiceImpl handles registration with uniqueness validation, JWT-based login, profile retrieval, and password changes by orchestrating repositories, the password encoder, and the JWT token provider.

tour.title: Security & Authentication
tour.description: JwtTokenProvider generates and validates HMAC-SHA JWTs with email as the subject and a role claim. SecurityConfig wires up the full Spring Security filter chain: disables CSRF, enables CORS, sets stateless sessions, defines endpoint-level authorization rules, and injects the JwtAuthenticationFilter. A Redis-backed RateLimitFilter protects login/register endpoints from brute force attacks.

tour.title: REST API Controllers
tour.description: REST controllers expose the service layer to HTTP clients. AuthController handles /api/auth/register, /api/auth/login, /api/auth/me, and password changes — the gateway every user interacts with first. LessonController provides CRUD endpoints for lessons with authentication context, serving as the primary content API consumed by the frontend's lesson listing and detail views.

tour.title: Frontend Entry & Routing
tour.description: main.js is the Vue 3 application entry point that creates the app, installs Pinia for state management, registers Vue Router, and imports global CSS. App.vue provides the shell layout with Header, Footer, and a router-view outlet. The router defines all frontend routes with authentication guards and lazy-loaded views for lessons, login, register, profile, leaderboard, and vocabulary search.

tour.title: Frontend Views
tour.description: Home.vue is the Bauhaus-styled landing page with a geometric hero section and feature cards highlighting lessons, flashcards, and achievements. Lessons.vue lists all published lessons with level-based filtering (All, Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced) and loading/error states. LessonDetail.vue is the most complex view with tabbed navigation for vocabulary flashcards, grammar explanations, and practice exercises with submission handling and feedback.

tour.title: State Management & API Integration
tour.description: The Pinia auth store manages user login state, token persistence via localStorage, profile fetching, and logout — connecting the frontend authentication flow to the AuthController from Step 9. api.js creates a configured Axios instance with an auth token interceptor and a 401 redirect interceptor. authService.js wraps the specific /api/auth/* calls, completing the round-trip from UI to backend.
